labels.message: `this.promise.then` at line 27 returns a promise that is neither awaited nor given a rejection handler
labels.reason: Arbiter ruling (Fable, upheld on review): the floating then() at line 27 returns a promise that rejects if any listener throws, and CancelToken.subscribe is public API, so a user listener's error becomes an unhandled rejection that also skips the remaining cancel listeners.

checks.reason: Line 27 calls the native `this.promise.then(cb)` (the override comes later, at line 39) and discards the derived promise with no catch; the source promise can never reject, but the derived one rejects if `token._listeners[i](cancel)` at line 33 throws, and because `subscribe()` is public API (index.d.ts:603) that listener can be user code, so the throw becomes an unhandled rejection and the loop stops before the remaining listeners run.
`this.promise.then((cancel) => {...})` at line 27 is a floating promise with no catch, so a throwing listener in the callback would produce an unhandled rejection.

labels.reason: The update hook returns a promise that rejects when the synchronous re-render (updateSync) throws; with no rejection handler the error is unhandled and resolve(node) is never called, so the pending update never settles.

checks.reason: `context[2](...).then(() => resolve(node))` is neither awaited, returned nor given a rejection handler, so a rejection from the async update hook is unhandled.
